$schema-note: Every difference between a v9 frame and the implementation lands in exactly one class. Gate B reads this file and enforces the rules below — the classification is not advisory prose.

classes.MUST-FIX: Clearly violates v9 with no functionality or accessibility reason. Implement the v9 design exactly. BLOCKS its frame until closed. No approval needed to fix — fixing toward v9 is the mandate.
classes.APPROVED-DEVIATION: Existing functionality or accessibility requires something different from v9. DO NOT MODIFY until the owner explicitly approves. Blocks its frame while status is pending.
classes.PRODUCT-DECISION: The v9 HTML specifies a different workflow or different copy, and choosing between them is the owner's call, not an engineering one. DO NOT MODIFY until the owner explicitly approves. Blocks its frame while status is pending.
classes.NOT-BUILT: The surface or its server support does not exist yet. Leave untouched until its assigned migration task runs. Does not block a frame for a defect it cannot have.

deviations.summary: Geist Sans/Mono retained instead of the spec's system font stack
deviations.reason: The system stack renders as SF Pro on iOS and Roboto on Android — two different products. Sizes, weights and tracking follow the spec exactly.
deviations.measuredCost: Geist runs ~5% wider per glyph at 800. Measured on frame 07 at the spec's own values (27px/800/-0.02em, 22px gutters, 326px available): Geist 336px vs the system stack 320px. So the .ob-q question WRAPS TO TWO LINES where frames 07 and 08 set it on one.
deviations.openQuestion: See deviation 19 — the wrap is tracked separately so it can be ruled on without reopening the font choice.

deviations.summary: design-system.md §12.1 reversed: ambient wash allowed app-wide, mascot allowed on working screens
deviations.reason: The v9 spec reverses two Phase-2.6 rules. Its own mascot law bans Odo only from money and safety surfaces.

deviations.summary: 5 tabs → 4 tabs + /more hub
deviations.reason: The v9 nav is 4 tabs plus the orb in every frame. No route removed.

deviations.summary: WebAuthn descoped pre-launch; frame 06 out of scope
deviations.reason: Browser inconsistency and support burden outweigh the MVP security delta.

deviations.summary: Patient tab renamed "Tooth Map" → "Teeth"
deviations.reason: Matches the spec's .ptabs row.
deviations.note: APPROVED BUT NOT YET IMPLEMENTED — app/(app)/patients/[id]/page.tsx still reads 'Tooth Map'. Task 22 owns the change.

deviations.summary: Clinic creation kept as 3 steps; the frame shows a single screen
deviations.reason: The single screen drops hours and profile capture. Feature parity outranks fidelity.
deviations.openQuestion: AMBIGUOUS AS WRITTEN. The frame's model is one QUESTION at a time ("What's your clinic called?" → "Next · City"), while our step 1 holds six fields. "Keep 3 steps" does not settle whether step 1 should be one question or six fields — those are different claims.
deviations.ruling: KEEP the 3-step workflow, but redesign each step to the v9 one-question-at-a-time pattern with a destination-labelled CTA. Do NOT collapse the required data collection. Step 1 must not remain a dense six-field form.
deviations.fixedIn: Step 1 now asks ONE QUESTION AT A TIME — five screens on one route: name -> contact -> address -> city+state -> pincode+GST, each with the `.field` hero input and a CTA naming its destination. All three steps and all seven fields survive; only the pacing changed. The question list lives in lib/ds/wizard with a test asserting every key of stepBasicsSchema appears exactly once, so re-pacing can never silently drop a field. Back walks the questions before leaving the step, so one tap no longer discards four answers. 8.7% -> 5.1%.

deviations.summary: No summoned numeric keypad on /phone
deviations.reason: The page has always used the native keyboard; building a pad adds a surface rather than migrating one.
deviations.ruling: KEEP the keypad. Implement v9 visually and behaviourally, preserving phone validation and rate-limit logic.
deviations.fixedIn: Built as `NumericKeypad` from the spec's `.keypad`/`.key` CSS: 48px keys, radius 12, white, 0 3px 10px shadow, 19px/600 digits over 8.5px/700 letter rows, ghost bottom corners. Real <button>s, so it is keyboard-reachable and screen-reader announced, and the native keyboard still works underneath. It only produces digits — IndianPhone.safeParse still gates the CTA and rate-limit handling is untouched.

deviations.summary: /more shows 3 module tiles for a doctor, not 4
deviations.reason: canAccess('/billing','DOCTOR') is false. Rendering it would leak a permission — an access-control requirement, not a style choice.
deviations.ruling: APPROVED — 3 tiles. RBAC determines available actions; no inaccessible fourth tile for symmetry.

deviations.summary: /lab/new kept as a page; the frame shows a sheet
deviations.reason: Feature parity.
deviations.ruling: USE the sheet presentation for lab creation. Preserve every existing field, validation rule, API call and workflow. Presentation only.

deviations.summary: Patient detail keeps 5 tabs (Media has no frame)
deviations.reason: Feature parity — Media must not disappear.
deviations.ruling: APPROVED — keep 5 tabs including Media.

deviations.summary: Mascot rendered on /role; frame 07 has none
deviations.reason: Introduced without cause during migration and never flagged.

deviations.summary: /role used tap→navigate; frame 07 is select→sticky CTA "Continue as doctor"
deviations.reason: A different interaction model, shipped unflagged.

deviations.summary: Phone number masked to "+91 ••••• 0001"; frame 04 shows it in full
deviations.reason: Shoulder-surfing protection on a screen a patient may see. A workflow/privacy choice, not styling.
deviations.ruling: APPROVED — keep masking. Recorded as a deviation FROM v9, not a match to it: frame 04 shows the number in full ("Sent to +91 98401 23456 · Edit") and v9 specifies no masking anywhere. The intent in both the table ("KEEP masking") and the prose ("do not expose the complete phone number") is unambiguous, so the mask stays and the departure is on the record.

deviations.summary: An explicit "Verify" button; frames 04/05 auto-submit on the sixth digit
deviations.reason: Accessibility: SMS autofill does not always fire, and a screen-reader or keyboard user needs an explicit submit target. Auto-submit alone leaves no way to retry a corrected code.
deviations.ruling: APPROVED — keep the Verify button. Functional UI is not removed to reduce a pixel percentage.

deviations.summary: A wrong code clears the six boxes; frame 05 keeps the digits inside crit outlines
deviations.reason: No functionality or accessibility reason to clear. The frame keeps the digits precisely so the user can see and fix the typo; clearing forces a full re-entry.
deviations.fixedIn: Gate B remediation — MUST-FIX pass

deviations.summary: /welcome carousel has 4 slides with different copy, a Skip link and language chips; frame 02 is slide 1 of 3 with none of those
deviations.reason: The frame's slide-1 copy ('Speak. Odovox writes the record.') is the product's opening promise. Which pitch opens the app is a product call.
deviations.ruling: MATCH v9. Frame 02 has THREE dots, NO Skip link and NO language chips, and its note reads "3 swipeable value dots; CTA skips them" — so the Skip behaviour IS the CTA, which goes straight to /phone. Implement: v9 slide-1 copy, 3 slides, no separate Skip link, no chips, CTA always "Continue with phone".
deviations.fixedIn: 3 slides with frame 02's slide-1 copy verbatim, no Skip link (the CTA carries that job, per the frame's own note "CTA skips them"), no language chips, 3 dots. Layout re-anchored to the frame's top-down flow — 56px above Odo, 18px to the question, dots 20px under the body, CTA at the floor — replacing a vertically centred group that sat ~70px low. 10.0% -> 2.8%.

deviations.summary: /clinic-join is a two-field form + explicit "Find clinic"; frame 09 is one hero code field with a live check and a clinic preview
deviations.reason: Two things at once: the joiner's name is feature parity (the request records who is asking), and the lookup model differs (explicit press vs validate-as-you-type).
deviations.ruling: APPROVED — keep the two-field lookup. Recreate the v9 visual treatment around the existing reliable workflow.

deviations.summary: The Odo mascot artwork was not the spec's #odo-body symbol
deviations.reason: The spec draws an outline tooth with lime blush ovals; the app drew a filled grey tooth with no blush. Systemic.
deviations.fixedIn: Gate B remediation

deviations.summary: The .ob-q question wraps to two lines where frames 07 and 08 set it on one
deviations.reason: A measured consequence of approved deviation 1, not an independent defect — the app matches the spec's values exactly. Closing it means altering one of the spec's own numbers.
deviations.openQuestion: (a) accept the wrap, (b) drop the question to ~25.5px, or (c) tighten question tracking to about -0.0355em.
deviations.ruling: MATCH the v9 wrap. Verify in order: font family, weight, container width, size, line height; use letter-spacing only if needed.
deviations.fixedIn: Applied in the ruling's own order. Items 2-5 already matched the spec exactly (800 weight, 326px container, 27px, 1.15 leading), and item 1 is approved deviation 1, so letter-spacing was the only remaining lever: new --tracking-question token at -0.036em, scoped to the .ob-q heading alone. The rest of the app keeps the spec's -0.02em. Verified in the browser: "How will you use Odovox?" now renders on ONE line at 326px.

deviations.summary: A lime focus ring on the .field; the frame's focused field has none
deviations.reason: Accessibility. Removing focus indication to win pixels is a real regression for keyboard users.
deviations.ruling: APPROVED — keep the focus ring. Make it restrained and consistent with the v9 system.

deviations.summary: A "By continuing you agree to our terms." line; frame 03 has none

deviations.summary: No .mic-a affordance on /phone
deviations.reason: useDictation presigns an upload and calls an AUTHENTICATED transcription endpoint; /phone is pre-login by definition. Needs an unauthenticated dictation route that does not exist. A mic that does nothing is worse than no mic.

deviations.summary: A "Wrong code. N attempts left." toast on top of the frame's inline message
deviations.reason: The frame reports the failure once, inline. The toast reports it twice — but it also carries the remaining-attempts count, which is information the frame does not show and which warns of lockout. Dropping it loses that warning.
deviations.ruling: KEEP the attempts-left toast. Restyle to the v9 visual language.

deviations.summary: WITHDRAWN — false finding. Resend already unlocks immediately on a wrong code.
deviations.reason: The verify catch already calls setSecondsLeft(0), so "Resend code" renders at once, exactly as frame 05 specifies. The first review read "Resend in 1:00" off a capture taken BEFORE the error state was reached — the A5 prepare step was silently failing, so the screenshot was of the clean OTP screen. Fixing the prepare step invalidated the finding.

deviations.summary: A dotted texture sits behind the resend area; frames 04/05 have none
deviations.reason: Pure decoration with no functional or accessibility role.

deviations.reason: All four are v9 elements the app simply does not render. Independent of deviation 6 — keeping three steps says nothing about dropping the frame's furniture from step 1.

deviations.summary: A 'Recent' section on /home; frame 13 has none

deviations.summary: A back chevron in the /consult header; frame 21 has none
deviations.reason: /consult is not one of the four dock tabs — it is reached from Flow's 'Continue consultation'. Removing back would strand anyone who arrived that way. Navigation, not decoration.

deviations.reason: There is no outstanding-balance filter on the API — PatientFilter is all/in_chair/due_today/lab_pending/recent. A chip that silently returned the unfiltered list would be worse than its absence, so it is not rendered. Needs a server filter.

deviations.summary: An "All patients · N" section header above the list; frame 32 goes straight to the card

deviations.summary: Free-form voice intent routing has no surface in the app since ruling #30 removed VoiceCommandHero
deviations.reason:
VERIFIED, not assumed. `routeVoiceCommand` (lib/voice/intent-router.ts) had exactly one caller — VoiceCommandHero — and that component now has none. The orb is a voice affordance in NAME (mic icon, hold menu) but not in behaviour: nav-dock.tsx:59 is `onTap={() => router.push(action.href)}` and voice-menu.tsx:87 is `router.push(row.href)`. Neither captures speech. So "say what you want, get routed" is gone from the running app while intent-router.test.ts keeps passing and makes it look healthy.

Ruling #30's stated rationale was 'the dock orb remains the single global voice affordance'. That premise is true of the icon and false of the behaviour, so the ruling was likely made without this being visible.
deviations.foundBy: peer session during a cross-session coordination check
options: (a) Wire dictation into the orb tap, or add a sixth 'Say something else…' row to the frame-78 menu — keeps ruling #30 and loses nothing.
(b) Accept the loss: delete VoiceCommandHero, intent-router.ts and its tests as dead code. Honest, but ends free-form voice.
(c) Keep it recorded as an open decision, which by this file's own `rule` reopens Task 13 until it is resolved.
deviations.doNot: Do NOT resolve this by deleting the router without a ruling — that converts an open question into a silent capability loss.
deviations.alsoAffects: /today (frame 50) has the same shape. Frame 50's header carries ONLY an avatar — no ＋ — so the frame relies on the dock orb for actions. Our floating FabMenu therefore duplicates the orb and overlaps 'Recent activity'. On /home and /patients the fix was to move the dial onto a header ＋ the frame actually draws; frame 50 draws none, so /today cannot be fixed the same way. Resolving #41 by wiring the orb to the speed dial fixes BOTH the missing voice routing and this overlap. Folded in here rather than opened as a separate decision — it is one question, not two.
deviations.ruling: APPROVED — wire the dock orb as the single global floating action/voice affordance, preserving BOTH voice command routing and speed-dial actions. /today must not render a duplicate FAB. Do not remove voice functionality to simplify the UI.
deviations.fixedIn:
The orb hold-menu gains a sixth row, "Say something else…", which CAPTURES SPEECH rather than navigating (href: null) and hands the transcript to routeVoiceCommand. That restores the exact capability ruling #30 removed — an unclear command still lands in patient search with the transcript rather than a dead end. `routeVoiceCommand` has a live caller again.

Reception keeps everything /today's FAB carried: "Add walk-in" and "Take a payment" are now role-gated rows in the same menu (RECEPTIONIST and ADMIN — on a small clinic's single device the admin IS the front desk). Walk-in routes to /today?walkin=1, which opens the existing sheet on arrival; new patient, book and lab case were already menu rows.

/today no longer renders a FabMenu. v9-50 7.0% -> 6.1%.

One existing test asserted the menu held EXACTLY five rows. Rather than delete it, it now asserts frame 78's five intents are present and in order — the guarantee it existed for — so it still fails if one is dropped or reordered.

Also caught by building rather than typechecking: /today now reads useSearchParams, which Next requires inside a Suspense boundary. `pnpm build` failed where typecheck passed. Boundary added; bundle unchanged at 103 kB.

deviations.summary: Frame 26's second action, "Keep audio · review later", does not exist
deviations.reason: Frame 26 offers 'Keep audio · review later' beneath 'Try again'. That implies a deferred-review queue: audio parked on the device, surfaced later as work outstanding. No such queue exists, and inventing one inside a UI task would be a product feature built without a spec. The screen ships 'Record again instead' in that slot, which is the existing capability and must not be removed (FAILED retains the blob, so re-record is a real alternative to retrying the upload). Both actions honour the frame's own note, 'Failure never loses audio'.
deviations.openQuestion: Should the deferred-review queue be built? It needs its own surface (where does parked audio appear?), a retention rule, and a story for audio that never gets reviewed. Recommend scheduling it with the consult-queue work rather than folding it into Task 16.

deviations.summary: The transcript was shown under the processing bar; the dentist must not see the pipeline
deviations.reason: Frame 25's mock is mid-upload, so it has no transcript to show — it does not decide against one. Our TRANSCRIBED state HAS the doctor's own words back, and it is the first proof the audio survived. Rendered quietly under the bar rather than dropped.
deviations.ruling: DROP the transcript from the processing state. The dentist-facing model is RECORD → Processing → AI Review. No uploading, transcription, extracting, provider names, SSE or internal stage vocabulary reaches the UI. One polished loading state: Odo, a concise message, an elegant progress treatment, nothing else.
deviations.fixedIn: Removed from `ProgressStrip`. The transcript is still carried by the TRANSCRIBED state and still reaches the extraction and review workflow — only the dentist-facing processing UI stops rendering it.

deviations.summary: Frames 23-26: 23 and 24 now captured; 25 and 26 still not driven
deviations.reason: These are states inside a live consultation, not routes. Capturing them needs a shot that creates a real consultation, grants the microphone and drives the store through its actual transitions. The harness now launches Chromium with a fake capture device and grants the microphone permission — half the driver — but the remaining half (seeding an in-chair patient and starting a consultation per run) is real work and mutates data. NOT faked: no production state was invented to produce a screenshot, which is why these four frames report NOT-CAPTURED rather than a number.
deviations.fixedIn:
The driver works and is real: Chromium launches with a fake capture device, the shot taps Record (starting an actual consultation), taps the mic, and the consult store walks its own machine. D2-recording and D3-paused capture RECORDING and PAUSED with no injected state.

D4-processing and D5-failed still fail: the click after 'Finish' times out, so STOPPED is not being reached the way the driver expects. Not diagnosed yet. NOT worked around by faking the state.

deviations.summary: The recording screen is restyled but not recomposed to frame 23
deviations.reason:
Visual inspection of the side-by-side, not the percentage. Frame 23 is: a patient strip at the top (avatar, name, age/sitting Minis, allergy in crit) with the REC chip opposite; a LARGE timer; a central lime mic orb with concentric rings; the complaint as a chip beneath it; and two CIRCULAR buttons with labels below (Pause, and a dark Finish with a check). Ours keeps the old composition — a five-bar waveform, a small mono timer, and two pill buttons — with v9 tokens applied to it.

The controls and states are right; the composition is not. 8.5% and 7.1% are mostly this.
deviations.ruling: OWNER (verbatim): "#45 remains CLOSED: the recording screen must use the V9 structural composition: patient strip + large timer + central recording orb/rings + complaint context + low circular controls."
deviations.fixedIn: apps/web/components/voice/recorder.tsx recomposed to frame 23's measured geometry (56px zero-padded tabular timer, 180px ring stack at insets 0/21/42 around a 92px lime orb, complaint chip beneath, two 62px labelled IconCircles pinned low); the patient strip moved onto apps/web/app/(app)/consult/[id]/page.tsx and now spans frames 23-26. PAUSED recolours the rings and swaps the primary rather than relayouting, per frame 24. The old waveform composition and the Waveform component are gone.

deviations.summary: A rejected consultation made its visit permanently un-recordable — the root cause of #44
deviations.reason: POST /consultations returns the EXISTING consultation for a visit whatever its status (consultations.ts findUnique on visitId). Once a doctor taps Re-record — which posts /consultations/:id/reject and sets status REJECTED — and then leaves the screen or the app reloads, tapping Record for that patient in the queue re-enters the same REJECTED consultation. deriveStateFromView returns {kind:'REJECTED'} and the consult page router.replace's back to /consult. The doctor taps Record, is bounced to the queue, and the visit can never be recorded again — silently, with no error. Reproduced against the live stack: D2/D3/D4/D5 capture now dead-ends on the queue screen.
deviations.ruling: APPROVED AS MUST-FIX (owner, verbatim): "A REJECTED consultation represents a rejected recording/processing attempt, NOT a permanently unusable visit. POST /consultations for a visit that already has a REJECTED consultation must reuse that existing consultation and reset it to PENDING_REVIEW so the doctor can record again... The rejection itself MUST remain durable in AuditLog via CONSULTATION_REJECTED. Do NOT drop the unique Consultation.visitId constraint. Do NOT create a second consultation record for the same visit as part of this fix. Do NOT remove or weaken the audit trail."
deviations.fixedIn: apps/api/src/routes/consultations.ts — POST /consultations resets a REJECTED consultation in place: status PENDING_REVIEW, and every field that is the rejected ATTEMPT's own output cleared (structuredData, rejectedById, rejectedReason, rawTranscriptEnc, audioUrl, audioStorageKey, audioDurationMs, languageCode, provider, sttLatencyMs, extractionLatencyMs, safetyWarnings). The schema was inspected per the ruling: those are precisely the transient/derived columns of one recording. Patient, Visit, ConsultationEdit and AuditLog are untouched, the unique visitId constraint stands, and no second row is created. A CONSULTATION_REOPENED audit row records the reset. Regression: apps/api/test/consultation-reject-then-rerecord.test.ts covers all eight required proofs. Clearing the transcript and audio key is the safety half — without it the next take would inherit the abandoned recording's dictation.

deviations.summary: The recording strip shows age but not the sitting number ("36 · S2")
deviations.reason: Frame 23's identity Mini reads '36 · S2' — age and which sitting of the active plan this is. ConsultationContext (packages/types/src/visit.ts) carries no plan or sitting; adding it means a join on the consultation-context endpoint. The queue snapshot already gained `activePlan` for the /home hero, so the shape exists, but widening a second endpoint is API work outside a recording-UI task and the Task 16 brief forbids changing API contracts absent a blocking bug. Age renders correctly; the sitting is simply absent, not wrong.
deviations.openQuestion: Add `activePlan` to ConsultationContext so the recording strip can show the sitting? Recommend folding it into the task that owns the patient-context card rather than Task 16.

deviations.summary: Auto-pause on interruption — frame 24's "Paused automatically for a phone call"
deviations.reason: Frame 24's banner reads 'Paused automatically for a phone call · audio safe on this phone'. Nothing in the recorder listens for an interruption — no visibilitychange handler, no MediaRecorder pause on an audio-session interrupt — so every pause today is one the doctor pressed. The banner ships in the frame's amber treatment and position with honest copy ('Paused · audio safe on this phone') rather than claiming a phone call that did not happen. Fabricating the cause on a clinical screen is worse than saying less.
deviations.openQuestion: Build auto-pause on interruption? It is a real robustness win — an incoming call currently keeps the recorder running and captures the call instead of the consultation — but it needs its own investigation of iOS/Android audio-session behaviour in a PWA. Recommend a task of its own; the banner copy becomes frame 24's verbatim once it exists.

deviations.summary: Task 17's own file list and its zero-pixel rule contradicted each other; resolved in favour of the rule
deviations.reason: Task 17 required (a) zero pixel change, (b) a split into six named files including `summary-bento.tsx` and `record-prose.tsx`, and (c) five regression tests passing untouched. All three cannot hold. (b) names post-Task-18 anatomy — the bento's TOOTH/FEES/NEXT-SITTING are currently three of seven sequential rows, so creating those files means reordering the DOM, violating (a). And (c) is impossible with any split at all: the tests grep the source TEXT of verification-card.tsx, so moving code breaks them without changing behaviour. Resolved in favour of the zero-pixel rule, which is the task's actual purpose.
deviations.ruling: Self-resolved under the standing rule that a task closes no open decision of its own, and that the plan is fixed in the same change when it contradicts itself. The plan file now carries both corrections inline.
deviations.fixedIn: Split follows today's seams: field-row · identity-header · record-fields · medicine-list · lab-case-block · safety-banner · actions. Test source-loading widened to the directory via test/regression/verification-sources.ts with assertions byte-identical, except two that described JSX shapes the split turned into a prop and into data (both keep their intent). That widening also CLOSED a hole: identity-from-patient-only would otherwise have kept passing while guarding one file out of seven. Proof of zero pixel change is a byte-identical PNG hash for D6-verify before and after (fc0de187146092729350deb98d098cfc), not a diff percentage. Logic that had leaked into JSX moved to lib/consult/card-view.ts with 9 new tests — including that a mistyped tooth number is dropped rather than coerced.

deviations.summary: Frame 27's "Swap → Azithro 500" — no drug-substitution knowledge base exists
deviations.reason: The frame resolves an allergy conflict by swapping to a NAMED alternative antibiotic, and frame 28 shows the result ('swapped for Amoxicillin · allergy-safe'). Nothing in the app knows that azithromycin is the penicillin-safe substitute: SafetyWarning carries code, message, field and detail — no alternative — and there is no substitution table anywhere in the API. Hardcoding one inside a UI task would be inventing prescribing advice, which is the single thing this product must never do. The conflict rail ships with the frame's full anatomy (red rail, red drug name, one factual line, inline action) and the action is 'Remove', which is the resolution the safety model actually recognises (isResolved: the flagged medicine is no longer prescribed). It says Remove rather than Swap so the doctor is never told the app chose a replacement drug.
deviations.openQuestion: Build drug substitution? It needs a clinical data source, an owner for its correctness, and a decision about liability — the app would be suggesting a specific prescription. Recommend a dedicated task with clinical sign-off, not a migration task.

deviations.summary: The FINDINGS and PROCEDURE prose sections have no extraction fields behind them
deviations.reason: Frames 27-30 set the record as three narrative sections — FINDINGS, PROCEDURE, INSTRUCTIONS. ClinicalExtraction has exactly one free-text field, `notes`, which is where dictated patient advice lands and maps cleanly to INSTRUCTIONS. There is no findings field and no procedure narrative; producing them means new schema fields plus new Gemini prompt work, i.e. changing clinical extraction from inside a restyle. PaperBlock ships and renders the sections that have data; sections without data are omitted rather than filled with generated prose.
deviations.openQuestion: Add `findings` and `procedureNarrative` to ClinicalExtraction and the clinical prompt? It is the difference between a structured summary and a record a dentist would actually keep. Recommend scheduling with extraction work, where the prompt and its tests live.

deviations.summary: Frame 27 greys out Confirm on an allergy conflict; today the doctor may override with an audited warning
deviations.reason: Frame 27 shows 'Confirm & save' disabled while the allergy conflict is unresolved, and the task brief repeats it. That is a CLINICAL POLICY change, not a visual one. Today allergy_conflict is an advisory warning, not a blocking error: the API's own prompt says 'Do NOT remove the prescription — flag it; the doctor decides', and confirming over a live warning is a supported, audited path (confirmedWithWarning -> CONSULTATION_CONFIRMED_WITH_WARNING). Disabling Confirm would remove a doctor's documented authority to prescribe against a flag they have judged — for example a recorded 'rash' that they know to be tolerable. Implemented as today: Confirm is gated by BLOCKING errors only, and the conflict is drawn loudly on the drug.
deviations.openQuestion: Should an unresolved allergy conflict HARD-BLOCK confirm, overriding the doctor? Recommend no — keep the override with its audit trail, since the alternative is a clinician unable to file a record they believe is correct. If yes, the API's warning/blocking classification must change too, so the two layers do not disagree.

deviations.summary: Frame 30 packs medicines into a half-width tile beside NEXT; one composition ships for all four states
deviations.reason: Frames 27/28/29 give medicines a full-width card, one row per drug. Frame 30 — a single medicine — instead shrinks it to a half-width tile next to a NEXT · CEMENTATION tile. Shipping both means the medicines section changes shape based on how many drugs were prescribed, so the same information lands somewhere different each consultation and a doctor cannot build a habit of where to look. Frame 29's requirement (seven medicines with the same anatomy as two) is explicitly about that consistency. The full-width card ships for all four states; the NEXT tile keeps its place in the bento above.
deviations.ruling: Self-resolved under the standing rule that no task closes with an open decision of its own. Frame 29's own stated requirement decides it: anatomy must not change with list length.

deviations.summary: The conflict, resolved and seven-medicine states need clinical data no seeded recording produces
deviations.reason: All three are built and will render — the conflict rail, the resolved note with Undo and the seven-row list are implemented — but reaching them through the real application means a recording that actually dictates an allergy-conflicting drug (27/28) or seven medicines (29). The mock extractor produces neither from the harness's fake audio. Capturing them honestly needs seed data purpose-built for it: a patient with a recorded penicillin allergy plus a canned transcript that prescribes amoxicillin. That is a harness/seed task, not a UI one, and faking the state to get a screenshot is explicitly forbidden.
deviations.openQuestion: Add a seeded 'conflict demo' patient + canned transcript so 27/28/29 can be captured and regression-tested? Recommend yes — these are the states where the card earns its keep, and they are currently the least verified.

deviations.summary: The disabled-CTA line names what is actually missing instead of frame 35's static copy
deviations.reason: Frame 35 reads 'Name + phone unlock the button · everything else can wait'. CreatePatientInput requires name, phone, age AND gender, so a button enabled on name + phone would let the receptionist tap Create and collect a validation error instead of a patient — the precise failure Global Constraint 1 ('a disabled CTA always says why') exists to prevent. The line is computed from the fields still empty ('Name, phone, age and gender still needed') and shrinks as the form fills in, turning into 'Everything else can wait' once the API would accept it. That honours the constraint's intent more exactly than its own example copy does.
deviations.ruling: Self-resolved under the standing rule that no task closes with an open decision of its own. Global Constraint 1 decides it: the frame's static line would be false for this API.
deviations.fixedIn: apps/web/lib/patients/new-patient-form.ts with 7 tests, incl. age 0 (infants are patients).

deviations.summary: Optional fields move behind a 'More details' disclosure rather than being dropped
deviations.reason: Frame 35 shows only NAME, AGE, PHONE and FLAGS; frame 36 adds a collapsed 'More details' row. The form also carries blood group, address, chief complaint and allergies, none of which appear in either frame and none of which may be removed. They live inside the disclosure — every field the form ever had is still reachable. Two behaviours keep it from hiding anything that matters: the disclosure opens automatically when voice intake fills a field inside it, so dictated allergies are never filed away unreviewed; and GENDER stays on the main surface because the API requires it.
deviations.ruling: Self-resolved: a disclosure is not a deletion, and nothing required is inside it.

deviations.summary: The voice-filled intake form cannot be captured - the mock extractor returns nothing from fake audio
deviations.reason: Frame 36 is the form AFTER dictation, every voice-filled field wearing its lime spine. The spine, the touch-to-clear behaviour and the auto-opening 'More details' are all built. But capturing it means a real intake extraction, and Chromium's fake capture device produces audio the mock extractor parses into zero fields - verified by a shot that waited on the NAME input and timed out at 60s. Capturing it honestly needs a canned intake transcript in the mock provider, which is harness work; faking the form state is forbidden.
deviations.openQuestion: Add a canned intake transcript to the mock STT/extractor so voice-intake states can be captured and regression-tested? Same underlying gap as #55 - recommend one task for both.

deviations.summary: Voice intake claimed "Filled from your voice" over a form it had filled nothing into
deviations.reason: onIntake fired the success toast unconditionally. When the extractor understood nothing - a noisy room, a phone held wrong, a sentence it could not parse - the receptionist was told it worked, over a completely empty form, and sent to a Create button that would reject them. Found by READING the frame-36 capture: the toast was on screen above blank fields.
deviations.fixedIn: apps/web/app/(app)/patients/new/page.tsx - an extraction that sets no field now says "Couldn't catch that - try again, or type the details in." and returns early.

deviations.summary: Patient query hooks stay in lib/queries.ts rather than moving to lib/patients/queries.ts
deviations.reason: Task 21 asks for shared query hooks to move to lib/patients/queries.ts. They are already centralised — usePatient, useTeeth, usePlans, useMedia and the rest all live in lib/queries.ts, which is a cohesive module imported by several screens beyond patient detail. Pulling only the patient-shaped ones out would split that module along a line nothing else respects and churn every other importer for no behavioural gain. The task's actual goal — page.tsx stops being 958 lines of tabs and sheets — is met by the component split.
deviations.ruling: Self-resolved: the hooks are already in one place; the plan's path is not an improvement on it.

generalRule: Functionality, security, RBAC, accessibility and legal requirements are never removed for pixel-level fidelity. Where a deviation is approved, preserve the functionality and reproduce the v9 visual language around it. No additional deviation is created without asking first.
rule: EVERY COMPLETED TASK LEAVES ZERO OPEN PRODUCT-DECISION ITEMS FOR THAT TASK. Open decisions are raised and resolved within the task that surfaced them. They are never carried forward: a pile of 20-30 unresolved deviations at the end is a pile nobody can remember the reason for.
